Title: 90pct underage rape cases in Kelantan are consensual, says police
Article:
KOTA BARU: About 90 per cent of rape cases involving underage girls in Kelantan are believed to stem from consensual relationships rather than forced sexual acts, police said.
State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said, however, such cases were still investigated as statutory rape, regardless of whether the sexual activity was consensual.
"About 90 per cent of cases involving underage girls are consensual. They are not necessarily cases involving forced rape.
"However, when the girl is below the prescribed age, the case is still investigated under the relevant provisions of the law," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Kelantan Education Department and Police Coordination Meeting at the state education department office in Tunjong here today.
Also present was state education director Siti Norina Muhamad.
Yusoff said police were working closely with the Kelantan Islamic Religious and Customs Council (Maik) and the Kelantan Islamic Religious Department (Jaheik) to address the issue and reduce sexual offences involving minors.
"We have received good cooperation from Maik and Jaheik, and we can see the effectiveness of their efforts, including enforcement and awareness programmes," he said.
He said girls involved in rape cases were also referred to the religious authorities for appropriate guidance and counselling to create awareness and help prevent them from becoming involved in similar situations.
Asked whether any parents had been arrested for negligence or other offences for allegedly failing to prevent their children from becoming involved in such social issues, Yusoff said there had been no such arrests so far.
"So far, there have been none. However, a few parents have been called in for questioning," he said.
He said police were still investigating several cases involving possible parental neglect, including cases in Gua Musang and Tanah Merah.
"There are cases, but we are still investigating them. For example, there are cases in Gua Musang and Tanah Merah, but no one has been charged yet.
"We need to scrutinise the cases carefully before deciding whether charges should be brought," he said.
Yusoff said the priority was to identify the root causes of the problems and determine whether there had been any form of neglect within the family that could have affected the children.
"The main issue is that we need to know what the actual problem is so that it can be addressed at the family level.
"We need to determine whether there was neglect that affected the children," he said.
He said prosecution should be considered as a last resort, as legal action against parents could have wider implications for the family.
"This is the last option because the prosecution process itself could affect the family," he said.

Title: Twenty-nine illegal immigrants fined up to RM10,000
Article:
PASIR MAS: Twenty-nine undocumented migrants were fined between RM1,000 and RM10,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to illegal entry, overstaying and misuse of passes.
The accused, including three women, pleaded guilty before Sessions judge Zulkpli Abdullah.
They were charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering and remaining in the country without valid travel documents, Section 15(1)(c) for overstaying, and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963 for misuse of passes.
Of the 29, 15 were charged under Section 6(1)(c), 13 under Section 15(1)(c) and one under Regulation 39(b).
The court fined the 15 RM6,000 each, in default two months' jail. The remaining 13 were fined RM10,000 each, in default three months' jail, while one was fined RM1,000, in default one month's jail.
The migrants were from Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia.
Some of the accused, speaking through a court interpreter, appealed for leniency.
Siti Khaidijah Khairuddin prosecuted, while the accused were unrepresented.
They were detained by the Immigration Department during a series of operations in Kota Baru and Bachok on July 22, 23 and 24.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RXZ gatherings: Dr Dzul urges convoy organisers to strengthen rider safety measures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Organisers of mega motorcycle gatherings have a moral responsibility to ensure the safety of every participant, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Expressing concern over accident cases involving participants of the recent RXZ Members 8.0 gathering, including fatal crashes, as well as recurring fatalities reported in previous editions of the event, Dzulkefly said such incidents were "deeply worrying".
"To the organisers of such mega convoy programmes, I support your good intentions and the spirit of camaraderie that you seek to foster.
"However, the repeated fatal accidents from the first edition until the recent RXZ Members 6.0 event are deeply worrying.
"My suggestion is that responsible riding messages and road safety advocacy must be made a mandatory agenda in every event, so that unnecessary loss of lives due to excessive speed does not happen again," he said in a statement.
He extended his condolences to the families of those killed in recent accidents.
Dzulkefly pointed out that road accidents remained one of Malaysia's major public health challenges, ranking as the fifth-highest contributor to premature deaths in the country.
Citing the Malaysia Road Fatality Index by the Transport Ministry, Dzulkefly said an average of 18 people were killed daily in road accidents nationwide, with motorcyclists accounting for 59 per cent of fatalities.
He said the impact of road deaths extended beyond the loss of lives, affecting families and the economy.
Based on the Value of Statistical Life (VSOL), he said the government incurred losses of at least RM3.12 million for every life lost.
"This is not merely a figure; it represents heads of families, young people who are the nation's hope, and productive human capital lost in an instant," he said.
Dzulkefly also highlighted the strain placed on the healthcare system whenever there was a sudden increase in road accidents, as hospital resources including blood supplies, imaging equipment, operating theatres and specialist teams had to be mobilised.
"This is the reality of our healthcare system. One per cent of the Health Ministry's workforce shoulders the responsibility of managing 99 per cent of Malaysia's population," he said.

Title: Natural gas tariff adjustment to raise Hartalega costs, ASP gains seen limited
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The impending natural gas tariff adjustment from October 2026 is expected to increase production costs for Hartalega Holdings Bhd, although discussions on passing the higher costs to customers are still ongoing.
Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) said on the export front, the current 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian glove exports to the US remains unchanged, providing some stability for local glove makers.
The research firm said Hartalega could see another round of average selling price (ASP) increases amid renewed Middle East tensions.
However, the firm said the earnings upside is likely to be less pronounced as customers are adopting a more disciplined procurement strategy this time.
It said customers have sufficient inventory levels, allowing them to take a wait-and-see approach instead of rushing to replenish stocks as they did during the March disruption.
Following a recent meeting with Hartalega's management, PublicInvest said the more measured purchasing behaviour suggests any earnings uplift would be less pronounced than during the previous supply disruption.
Despite the more cautious demand outlook, PublicInvest expects Hartalega's first-quarter financial year 2027 (Q1 FY27) results, due on Aug 4, to benefit from stronger ASPs recorded in May and June.
It maintained its earnings forecasts for FY27 to FY29.
Following the recent correction in Hartalega's share price, PublicInvest upgraded the stock to "Neutral" from "Underperform".

Title: BDO: Look beyond financial models as Malaysia's deal activity accelerates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian companies are scaling up investments in infrastructure, mergers and acquisitions (M&A), but boards risk paying a premium for assets if they focus too heavily on financial projections without adequately evaluating operational realities, an advisory firm said.
BDO Malaysia executive director of advisory Fang Li Wei said the surge in investments across digital infrastructure, logistics hubs and clean energy facilities is fuelling demand for acquisitions of newly operational assets as companies look to accelerate growth and expand scale.
However, many transactions fail to adequately address what he described as the "pre-investment execution gap", he said.
"This gap represents the high-risk mismatch where an asset is physically operational yet fundamentally struggles to meet its business plan or meet the volume projections promised in the initial investment case," Fang said.
He warned that buyers evaluating acquisitions primarily through financial metrics risk purchasing what he called a "spreadsheet illusion", where projected returns fail to materialise because of overlooked operational constraints.
"An asset can look pristine on a historic cash flow statement yet hide hidden operational or regulatory bottlenecks that cap its performance the moment control changes hands," Fang said.
Fang said inadequate pre-investment governance can expose companies to post-acquisition challenges, including slower-than-expected asset ramp-up caused by supply chain disruptions, network capacity constraints or technical shortcomings that were not identified during due diligence.
Such issues can also create cash flow mismatches as companies incur unplanned capital expenditure to resolve operational bottlenecks while continuing to service acquisition-related financing, putting pressure on working capital.
He added that weaker-than-expected cash generation during the early years of ownership could strain debt servicing and potentially require parent companies to inject additional equity to meet financing obligations.
"To protect capital and ensure long-term returns, boards and investment committees must demand that these pre-investment execution gap risks are mapped directly onto the financial model before final approval," Fang said.
He said investment assessments should be based on comprehensive commercial, operational and technical due diligence; advanced financial modelling and stress testing; and coordinated stakeholder management supported by robust contractual alignment.
Financial assessments, he said, should extend beyond historical earnings by independently validating production capacity, market demand, competitive dynamics and technology lifecycles.
Investors should also evaluate operational risks such as feedstock availability, labour shortages and technology obsolescence, and reflect those factors in valuations rather than relying solely on information provided by sellers or internal project teams.
Fang said financial models should also be stress-tested against downside scenarios, including tariff changes, construction cost inflation and project delays, to assess whether assets can continue meeting debt obligations under weaker operating conditions.
"A fragmented approach creates communication gaps, drives up transactional friction, and weakens corporate governance. Teams evaluating technical or commercial risks may not fully appreciate the interdependencies and implications of their findings and/or advice to legal advisers drafting the project documents," he said.
To address this, Fang said companies are increasingly seeking advisers capable of integrating technical, commercial, financial, tax and risk expertise under a single framework.

Title: Hap Seng Plantations favoured on yield, growth potential
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hap Seng Plantations Bhd remains a preferred pick among Malaysian plantation stocks, supported by strong fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production growth, attractive dividend yields and an undemanding valuation.
CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd maintained its "Add" call on the stock with an unchanged target price of RM3.35.
It noted that Hap Seng Plantations is trading at below 10 times its projected financial year 2026 (FY26) and FY27 price-to-earnings ratio, making it the cheapest stock under its Malaysian plantation coverage.
It said the plantation company is also expected to deliver dividend yields of more than six per cent over the next two years.
CGS International expects FY26 earnings to be supported by sector-leading FFB production growth and higher year-on-year crude palm oil (CPO) prices.
According to the firm, management has maintained its FY26 FFB production guidance of between 714,000 and 715,000 tonnes, representing growth of 16 to 17 per cent year-on-year.
The company's FFB output increased seven per cent in the first half of the year, accounting for 42 per cent of CGS International's full-year forecast.
The research firm is projecting a more conservative FY26 production growth of 13 per cent.
CGS International also highlighted Hap Seng Plantations' relatively lower cost pressures compared with industry peers, with the company securing its fertiliser requirements for 2026 in April and expecting fertiliser costs to increase by only five to 10 per cent year-on-year, compared with the 15 to 25 per cent rise anticipated for many plantation companies.
In addition, Hap Seng Platations may benefit from priority access to fertiliser supplies through its parent company, Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd, which operates a fertiliser trading business, it said.
Looking ahead, CGS International said the potential emergence of a strong El Niño weather pattern could weigh on FFB production in FY27 but may also boost palm oil prices.
For FY26, the firm forecasts the net profit to almost double to RM206 million from RM112.4 million in FY25 and stabilise to RM201 million in FY27, supported by higher production volumes and stronger palm oil prices.
Revenue is projected to increase to RM884.7 million in FY26 from RM702.4 million in FY25, before edging up to RM893.6 million in FY27.
The research firm identified stronger-than-expected dividend payouts and a sharp rise in CPO prices driven by El Niño-related supply concerns as potential catalysts for a re-rating of the stock.
However, higher production costs and weaker-than-expected sales volumes remain key risks.

Title: Kelantan police welcome Thai plan for 99km border fence
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan police have welcomed Thailand's plan to build a 99km barbed-wire fence along its southern border with Malaysia.
State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the move could help curb cross-border crime, smuggling and the movement of unwanted elements.
He said the proposed fence would complement Malaysia's efforts to strengthen security along the border and help prevent illegal cross-border movement.
"I recently read about their plan to build the fence and welcome the proposal by the Thai authorities.
"This is a good move as it can help curb all kinds of unwanted elements, smuggling and drug-related activities, including the movement of those involved in violence in southern Thailand," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Kelantan Education Department and Police Coordination Meeting at the state education department office in Tunjong here today.
Also present was state education director Siti Norina Muhamad.
Yusoff said Malaysia had also taken steps to strengthen border security by closing illegal routes.
"That is why Kelantan police have decided to close the illegal jetties along the border to prevent any kind of unwanted movement.
"The Malaysian government has also approved the construction of security walls and fences, and the project is currently under construction," he said.
Yusoff said the project was expected to be completed by 2029 at an estimated cost of RM3.04 billion.
The Thai Fourth Army Region recently announced plans to construct the barbed-wire fence from Tak Bai district through Sungai Golok to Waeng district in Narathiwat, covering about 99km of the mostly porous border.
The move is aimed at preventing suspected insurgents and smugglers from moving freely between Thailand and Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan polls outcome proves BN does not play racial politics, says Umno veep
Article:
TEMERLOH: The Negri Sembilan election outcome showed that voters prioritised administrative stability over racial sentiments, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
He said allegations that Barisan Nasional had used racial sentiments and identity politics throughout the campaign were unfounded, as the results showed that voters made their decisions based on the credibility of candidates and the need for a stable government.
"It is untrue (that BN used racial rhetoric). In Chennah, MCA's candidate Siow Kong Choon was fielded in a Malay-majority area, and the Malay community supported him. This proves that we are not racist and do not play up racial issues.
"If we had played up racial issues, the MCA candidate in Chennah would not have won the seat," he told reporters after opening the Pahang 1st gathering involving about 1,000 silat warriors in Temerloh today.
Yesterday, Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari attributed the coalition's defeat in the state election to the use of identity politics by BN and Perikatan Nasional.
He claimed that the
state polls
witnessed an extraordinary level of racial campaigning.
BN won 18 of the 36 state seats, while PN secured seven, allowing the two coalitions to form the new state government with a combined majority of 25 seats.
Meanwhile, Wan Rosdy, who is also  Pahang Menteri Besar, said the BN-PN cooperation had, for now, ended after the Negri Sembilan state election and that any future cooperation would be considered on a case-by-case basis.
"Currently, the cooperation only applies to Negri Sembilan, and we have not decided on similar cooperation elsewhere.
"Future cooperation, including in Melaka, will be decided by the leadership through discussions.
"As for now, we have settled Negri Sembilan, and Melaka might be next. We have not decided anything regarding Pahang," he said.
Earlier, Wan Rosdy was asked whether the BN and PN partnership would continue beyond the Negri Sembilan polls, including in preparation for the 16th General Election and whether it would involve Pahang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China's central bank pledges timely policy tool adjustment
Article:
BEIJING: China's central bank pledged to adjust monetary policy tools in a timely manner and facilitate panda bond issuance, a statement showed on Sunday.
The People's Bank of China (PBOC) will continue to implement an appropriately loose monetary policy and maintain ample liquidity, according to the readout of a work meeting on Saturday to map out the second half of the year.
The PBOC said it would "steadily promote the high-level opening of the financial market… advance domestic and international infrastructure cooperation, and enrich liquidity management and risk hedging tools."
It also pledged to "continue to financially support debt risk resolution of local government financing vehicles, and promote their market-oriented transformation."
In addition to supporting more overseas institutions issuing yuan-denominated bonds, known as panda bonds, the central bank said it would help Shanghai enhance cross-border finance and offshore financial services, while consolidating Hong Kong's position as an offshore yuan hub.
The meeting, chaired by PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng, followed a call by the Communist Party's Politburo on Thursday to accelerate fiscal spending on already budgeted infrastructure projects during the remainder of the year.
Data released last month showed the economy grew 4.3 per cent in the second quarter, its slowest pace in more than three years, missing the lower end of the full-year growth target of between 4.5 per cent and 5.0 per cent.
The Politburo, the country's top decision-making body, acknowledged the "difficulties and challenges facing the economy" at its meeting, state news agency Xinhua reported.
China must "accelerate the pace of fiscal expenditure" and enhance the flexibility and forward-looking nature of monetary policy, according to a summary of the discussion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Broken urinals, stagnant water raise concerns over hospital toilet conditions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several public toilet facilities at a hospital here were found to be in unsatisfactory condition, with some male restrooms experiencing maintenance issues including broken urinals, wet floors and stagnant water.
Checks by Harian Metro around noon today, after visiting hours began, found that the situation was most apparent at the men's toilets near the emergency ward and on the third floor of the hospital.
The checks found the facilities to be in a mediocre condition, with several aspects of hygiene and maintenance requiring attention.
The floors were wet, toilet bowls had standing water, while several fixtures appeared to require repairs.
At the third-floor men's toilet, a standing urinal was found to be broken and dislodged, with water pooling in the area. The damage had yet to be repaired.
Meanwhile, the women's toilets were found to be in better condition, although some sections of the floor were also wet.
A male patient, who declined to be named, said the condition of the men's toilet near the emergency ward was unsatisfactory and could pose a safety risk, particularly to patients and the elderly.
He said the slippery floors required him to be extra cautious whenever using the facility due to the risk of falling.
"The men's toilet is not in great shape. The floor is slippery and the urinals are also problematic, so it can be dangerous for patients using this toilet," he told Harian Metro.
A visitor, who wished to be known only as Mat, in his 50s, said the toilets were uncomfortable due to their small size, which caused users to queue during busy periods.
He added that hygiene and maintenance needed to be improved to make the facilities more comfortable for patients and visitors.
"The place is rather dirty and uncomfortable. On top of that, the toilet area is small, which means users have to wait when it gets crowded," he said.
Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) management had previously denied claims that its public toilets were dirty and poorly maintained, following the circulation of a viral video on Facebook.
Its director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K R Nair was quoted as saying that the hospital management had taken note of the allegations and conducted further investigations.
The investigation into all public toilet facilities under HKL's supervision found that the toilet featured in the viral video was not located within any facility managed by HKL.
The clarification came after a video alleging that a toilet at a public hospital in Kuala Lumpur was in a dilapidated condition, including overflowing urinals that had soiled the floor, went viral on social media, raising concerns over hygiene standards at the health facility.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thousands evacuated as Washington wildfires worsen
Article:
WASHINGTON: A fast-moving wildfire neared the US city of Spokane on Saturday, forcing thousands of residents to evacuate as Washington state declared an emergency over one of its worst fire seasons on record.
More than 200,000 acres were burning across the northwestern state during a record fourth consecutive year of statewide drought.
"Our record-setting drought and high winds are creating dangerous conditions across the state," Governor Bob Ferguson said in a statement, adding that most outdoor and agricultural burning were banned through the end of September.
"This year has already been one of our busiest wildfire years on record, and we just started August," said Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove.
A wildfire dubbed the Old Trails fire jumped the Spokane River on Saturday afternoon and crossed into the city, the Spokesman-Review newspaper reported.
Authorities issued the highest-level evacuation alert, "Go Now", for swathes of northern Spokane affecting thousands of people within city limits, according to the government's evacuation map.
The fire grew to more than 3,500 acres by 8.20pm (0320 GMT), according to the Spokesman-Review.
City officials did not report any injuries.
"When the sun sets and the sun rises, we are going to be in shock," Major General Gent Welsh told a news conference.
Emergency authorities set up a fire evacuation shelter at the Spokane Convention Centre.
Earlier in the day, the National Weather Service declared a "particularly dangerous situation" Red Flag Alert, which called the weather risk "extreme" across Eastern Washington.
The Washington National Guard said on X it was "rapidly mobilising units" to assist Spokane.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perhilitan relocates elephant troubling Gua Musang village
Article:
GUA MUSANG: The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) today successfully relocated a male elephant that frequently encroached into orchards and residential areas in Kampung Pulau Setelu here.
Kelantan Perhilitan director Wan Mohd Adib Wan Yusoh said the tusked male elephant is estimated to be between 15 and 18 years old.
He said the operation involved 19 personnel, including team members from the National Elephant Conservation Centre in Sungai Deka, Terengganu, and Kuala Gandah, Pahang.
"The elephant, named Awang Tar Setelu, was captured on July 23 and was successfully coaxed out today with the assistance of two female decoy elephants, Suria and Indah.
"The operation began at 9am today and concluded four hours later. The elephant will be released into its natural habitat," he said when contacted today.
Meanwhile, Kampung Pulau Setelu resident Zakaria Omar, 62, said villagers have faced threats from wild elephants for several years, sustaining losses to crops including oil palm, bananas and Musang King durians.
"Some elephants have even ventured as close as two to four metres from residents' houses, forcing us to remain constantly vigilant whenever we leave our homes," he said.
Mukim Bertam Barat federal village development and security committee chairman Mokhtar Dahari Ibrahim said the relocation has brought relief to more than 1,000 residents.
"After nearly two weeks of Perhilitan personnel being stationed here, the operation to relocate the wild elephant to another habitat was finally successful. The residents are relieved that the elephant has been captured.
"We hope no other elephants will come to this village. We would like to thank Perhilitan for working tirelessly to remove the wild elephant from our village," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shooter among three dead in Idaho shopping centre attack
Article:
BOISE: Three people died after a gunman opened fire in a shopping area in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, according to a city spokesman.
Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks told reporters the shooter was dead and the threat to the community was over.
An active shooter incident was reported at around 2.30pm local time (2030 GMT) near an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in a high-traffic commercial area, the city's public information coordinator, Josh Palmer, told Reuters.
About an hour later, "it was determined that the shooter was no longer a threat," Palmer said.
During a press conference, Hicks said he did not know the exact death toll, but Palmer told Reuters that three people were dead and at least two injured.
The shooter was among the dead, Hicks said. Police are working to identify the gunman and determine motives for the shooting, he said.
The Twin Falls Police Department said on Facebook that roads in the area and a nearby bridge were closed in the immediate aftermath of the report.
The town of about 47,400 people lies in the central Idaho region of Magic Valley. --REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: WestJet flight attendants go on strike after talks fall through, grounding flights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Flight attendants at Canada's WestJet went on strike on Sunday after failing to reach a deal with the country's second-largest carrier, grounding flights during the busy summer travel season.
The Canadian Union of Public Employees (CUPE), which represents 4,400 flight attendants at the carrier, majority-owned by Onex Corp, is seeking pay for its members from the time they check in until they clock out, which is not currently the case.
The strike follows a four-day work stoppage by flight attendants last August at larger rival Air Canada, highlighting broader efforts by flight attendants in Canada and the US to challenge a compensation structure that mostly pays cabin crew when an aircraft is in motion.
The union had given 72 hours' notice on Thursday to the airline signaling that a strike could come if talks failed to produce an agreement, following which WestJet issued a lock-out notice.
CUPE on Sunday said it had tried until the last minute to reach a deal but that "WestJet's offer did not go far enough."
"We are on strike because we believe we deserve better. We are ready to go back to the table to settle," said Alia Hussain, president of the WestJet component of the CUPE.
The airline, which has a domestic market share of about 30 per cent, confirmed the work stoppage and said it would refund or reaccommodate affected passengers. "We presented a proposal... to offer an hourly rate covering all time before and after flights, plus a double-digit wage increase in year one among other priorities the union raised. Unfortunately, it wasn't accepted," WestJet CEO Alexis von Hoensbroech said.
The airline canceled 309 flights through Sunday night in anticipation of the strike. It did so to "minimise the risk of stranding guests and aircraft."
The Canadian government intervened to stop the Air Canada strike last year, which was later defied by flight attendants. The union's WestJet division said it hoped the Canadian government would not interfere in the bargaining process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China flash flood death toll rises to 25
Article:
BEIJING: The toll from a flash flood in northwest China has risen to 25 dead, with 23 injured, state media reported Sunday a week after the disaster.
The flood ripped through the Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a tourist spot popular with day campers, on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injured.
The updated toll came as the country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event, Xinhua said.
Shuangshimen – in mountainous southern Gansu – is known for its natural stone arches, alpine meadows and mountain streams.
Videos of the flooding showed torrents of water surging through a valley where several tents and cars were parked.
China has been hit hard by extreme weather this summer, with large swathes of the country experiencing flooding.
In July, storms in Hubei province killed at least 11 people, while six died and 130,000 people were evacuated in the southern Guangxi region after several dams were breached following torrential rainfall.
The same month, a landslide in Gansu's Dangchang County, also in the province's south, killed 21.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HBA: Build-then-sell could break Malaysia's abandoned housing crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's long-debated Build-Then-Sell (BTS) model could offer a solution to the country's persistent abandoned housing crisis, but developers have remained reluctant to adopt a system that would require them to bear greater upfront financial risks.
As of June 30, Malaysia had 303 private housing projects classified as "sick" projects, involving 43,288 housing units with a gross development value (GDV) of RM40.25 billion.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), in a written reply published on the Parliament website, said 100 projects had been confirmed as abandoned, affecting 27,998 housing units and 14,961 buyers.
Selangor recorded the highest number of abandoned projects with 41, followed by Kelantan with 13 and Terengganu with 11.
The figures highlight the scale of the challenge facing Malaysia as the government seeks to address one of the country's most persistent housing problems – uncompleted homes that leave buyers financially burdened for years.
The launch of the National Housing Policy (NHP) 2026–2036 has renewed hopes among homebuyers, industry players and policymakers that Malaysia can finally resolve the issue of delayed and abandoned housing projects.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has set a target of achieving zero abandoned housing projects by 2030, supported by initiatives including the Housing Integrated Management System, the Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH) portal, the Electronic Sale and Purchase Agreement (eSPA) and stronger project monitoring.
However, the National House Buyers Association (HBA) said improving monitoring alone may not be enough unless Malaysia addresses the structural weakness in its housing delivery system.
HBA honorary secretary-general Datuk Chang Kim Loong said thousands of buyers have suffered financial hardship over decades, with many forced to continue servicing housing loans for unfinished homes while paying rent for alternative accommodation.
"The Minister's commitment is therefore both welcome and commendable. However, noble intentions alone cannot overcome structural weaknesses," said Chang.
He questioned whether Malaysia could realistically achieve zero abandoned housing projects by 2030 without shifting away from the current Sell-Then-Build (STB) model towards BTS.
"Malaysia has never lacked housing policies. Every administration has introduced comprehensive plans, transformation programmes and strategic blueprints promising greater affordability, better governance and stronger consumer protection.
"Yet abandoned projects continue to occur. This demonstrates an uncomfortable truth. Malaysia's housing problem is not a shortage of policies. It is a shortage of implementation," Chang said.
STB shifts risks to buyers.
"The National Housing Policy 2026–2036 offers the government another opportunity to demonstrate that this time is different. If the government truly believes that every Malaysian deserves a safe and secure home, then it must also ensure that every Malaysian is protected from financing risks beyond his or her control," Chang said.
Chang said the STB model remains the fundamental weakness behind the recurring issue.
Under the current system, developers sell properties before completion, while buyers sign Sale and Purchase Agreements and banks release loans progressively based on construction progress.
This means purchasers effectively finance housing projects before receiving completed homes, exposing them to significant risks if developers face financial difficulties.
When projects run into funding problems, construction may slow, developments can become distressed and some may eventually be abandoned. Yet buyers remain responsible for loan repayments on homes that have not been delivered.
"No amount of digital monitoring can change this fundamental allocation of risk," Chang said.
He argued that government efforts should focus on preventing abandoned projects rather than managing their consequences after buyers have already suffered.
BTS shifts risk back to developers.
According to Chang, the most effective preventive measure is the BTS model, where developers must complete substantial construction before receiving payment from purchasers.
"Prevention through BTS is far more effective than attempting to manage the consequences of sell-then-build," Chang said.
Under BTS, buyers purchase completed homes rather than promises, while development risks remain with developers who are better positioned to manage financing, construction and market risks.
"This encourages stronger financial discipline, discourages speculative developments and enhances public confidence," Chang said.
He added that Malaysia has discussed both the BTS 10:90 model and the more comprehensive BTS 0:100 model for years, with successive governments acknowledging their benefits, but implementation has remained elusive.
"If previous governments accepted BTS in principle but never implemented it, why should Malaysians believe that the latest National Housing Policy will finally deliver a different outcome while continuing to rely on the same STB framework?"
"BTS rewards responsible developers. It enhances market confidence. It improves industry credibility. Most importantly, it restores public trust. An industry respected for delivering completed homes will ultimately enjoy stronger and more sustainable long-term demand," Chang said.
Learning From Global Practices
Chang said Malaysia should also learn from international housing systems that place greater emphasis on protecting buyers and ensuring developers carry appropriate risks.
Countries such as Singapore have introduced strict licensing requirements, financial safeguards and regulatory oversight for developers, while Australia and several European jurisdictions have adopted stronger purchaser protection mechanisms and financing controls.
While no housing system is without challenges, Chang said the underlying principle is clear: development risks should primarily remain with developers rather than ordinary homebuyers.
"Malaysia should not hesitate to adopt international best practices where they provide better consumer protection," Chang said.
What Must the Government Do?
Chang said if the government sincerely intends to eliminate abandoned housing projects by 2030, several practical reforms deserve urgent consideration.
"Firstly, establish a clear timetable for progressively implementing mandatory BTS beginning with financially capable developers before extending it industry-wide.
"Secondly, tighten licensing requirements to ensure only developers possessing adequate financial strength and technical competence receive development licences.
"Thirdly, strengthen enforcement by prosecuting developers and company directors who repeatedly disregard statutory obligations.
"Fourthly, establish an Independent Housing Project Review and Monitoring Commission comprising representatives from the Ministry, financial institutions, professional bodies, consumer associations and the Attorney General's Chambers to identify troubled projects before they become abandoned.
"Fifthly, publish annual report cards measuring the National Housing Policy's performance using transparent indicators such as project completion rates, abandoned projects, enforcement actions and purchaser satisfaction.
"Finally, engage continuously with consumer organisations."
Chang said they possess decades of practical experience assisting victims of abandoned housing projects and can provide valuable policy feedback.
He said the transition from STB to BTS is not merely an administrative adjustment but a fundamental shift in philosophy, from asking house buyers to finance developers to requiring developers to earn purchasers' trust by delivering completed homes.
"Only then will Malaysia genuinely honour the spirit of the Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act as social legislation. Only then will house buyers receive the protection Parliament intended. And only then can the government confidently assure Malaysians that the era of abandoned housing projects has finally come to an end.
"Until that day arrives, the promise of "zero abandoned housing projects by 2030" will remain an aspiration rather than a guarantee," Chang said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13-year-old girl among seven arrested over knifepoint robbery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 13-year-old girl was among seven people arrested less than six hours after a man was allegedly robbed at knifepoint inside a condominium unit in Jalan Ampang here.
Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the case came to light after the victim lodged a police report at 9.02pm on July 31.
The 21-year-old victim claimed he was robbed by four unidentified men armed with knives while inside a unit at 3 Tower, Jalan Ampang.
"Following investigations, a team from the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters arrested five men aged between 22 and 38, and two females aged 13 and 19, at a parking area in Jalan Metro Pudu about 3am on Aug 1," he said in a statement.
Annas said police also recovered an iPhone 17 Pro believed to have been stolen during the incident.
"The suspects were remanded on Aug 1 and are being held at the Jinjang police lock-up to assist in investigations," he said.
The case is being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and robbery while armed with a weapon, offences which carry a maximum sentence of up to 20 years' imprisonment, a fine, whipping, or any two of the punishments upon conviction.
Police urged those with information on the case to contact the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters control centre at 03-9289 9222, the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan lockups not overcrowded despite drug arrest directive
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan police have assured that state lockups are not overcrowded despite a recent directive requiring every station chief to arrest at least one drug addict daily.
State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said concerns over lockup capacity should not hinder efforts to tackle the state's drug problem.
"There is no issue of overcrowded lockups. The capacity is sufficient. If we look at prisons, the situation is even more congested.
"If we only worry about gazetted capacity, the problem will never be resolved.
"But so far, there are no issues... Alhamdulillah," he told reporters here today.
Yusoff was
responding to reports
that he had instructed all station chiefs to detain at least one drug addict daily as part of efforts to curb criminal activities and drug abuse statewide.
He said the strategy was a comprehensive police initiative involving the entire force, rather than placing the responsibility solely on station chiefs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTD: No compromise on offences at RXZ Members gatherings
Article:
ALOR SETAR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) will step up enforcement against motorcycle gathering programmes, including RXZ Members, while holding engagement sessions with organisers amid recurring accidents linked to such events.
RTD director‑general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department does not prohibit motoring programmes, but participants must comply with traffic laws and vehicle technical regulations.
"We are not stopping such events as long as regulations are followed. If they are not, we will take action without compromise, especially against vehicle modification offences and violations of the law," he said after launching the MADANI Adopted Village and Adopted School programme here today.
He said accident investigations fall under the police, while RTD will take follow‑up action to avoid overlapping enforcement under the Road Transport Act.
Aedy Fadly stressed RTD will not compromise against participants who endanger other road users, noting public complaints about traffic congestion and reckless riding.
On the MyJPJ application, he said it now has nearly 15 million registered users, making it one of the most widely used government apps. Technical issues are normal for large‑scale platforms, but RTD is introducing new features and technologies in September.
He encouraged users to submit complaints or reports if they encounter problems with the app.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN morale soars after toppling PH heavyweights in Negri Sembilan polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's victory in two closely watched Negri Sembilan seats, Chennah and Linggi, has boosted the coalition's morale after it successfully defeated two high-profile Pakatan Harapan figures.
The
defeats
of DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke in Chennah and former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun in Linggi emerged as among the biggest surprises of the state election, with both seats attracting intense attention from political observers, party machinery and voters throughout the campaign.
Chennah had long been regarded as a DAP
stronghold
, with Loke holding the seat since 2013.
However, the MCA Youth chief Siow Kong Choon managed to pull off an upset victory, earning the label of a "giant killer" after defeating one of PH's most recognisable leaders.
Siow attributed his victory to the collective effort of his party machinery and supporters.
"This victory belongs to all the people of Chennah.
"Thank you for the mandate and trust given. I will carry this responsibility with full commitment to serve the people of Chennah," he said in a Facebook post.
Meanwhile, the contest in Linggi gained prominence after Aminuddin decided to leave his traditional stronghold of Sikamat to challenge BN in the Malay-majority constituency.
The move was seen as a strategic gamble by PH to expand its seat tally, but it also placed Aminuddin in one of the state's toughest battles as Linggi had remained under BN since the 1974 general election.
Despite his eight-year tenure as menteri besar and record in leading the state administration, Aminuddin failed to unseat incumbent Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, who retained the seat with an increased majority.
For Faizal, the victory marked a significant milestone in his political career.
"This success does not belong to me alone. This is our shared success.
"Thank you to all the BN leadership, the committed machinery and those with unwavering determination to keep Linggi as an Umno stronghold until today," he said in a statement on Facebook.
Faizal won the three-cornered contest with a majority of 2,976 votes, an increase from  the 1,461-vote majority he secured in the 2023 state election.
The results marked a major setback for PH, with Loke's defeat ending his 13-year representation of Chennah while Aminuddin's loss saw the former menteri besar relinquish one of the state's key seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan DAP backs Loke to remain state chairman
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan DAP has thrown its full support behind Anthony Loke to remain the party's state chairman, despite his offer to step down after failing to retain the Chennah state seat in the state election.
State DAP secretary Cha Kee Chin said the state committee had unanimously agreed that Loke should continue leading the party.
"We fully support Loke remaining at the helm because his leadership has been proven and is recognised as the best in the history of Negri Sembilan DAP.
"From winning just two seats in 2004, Loke's capable leadership has transformed Negri Sembilan DAP into a respected force admired by both allies and opponents," he said in a statement today.
"The defeats in the Chennah and Repah seats are certainly disappointing to us, but it is not Loke's fault, and he should not be held responsible for these losses," he said in a statement today.
Earlier, Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said during a press conference in Chennah that he was prepared to consider stepping down as state party chairman.
He said the decision was aimed at taking responsibility for DAP's performance in the state election, adding that he would raise the matter at the upcoming DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting.
In the Negri Sembilan election, Loke failed to defend the Chennah seat, which he had held for three terms.
Cha said Negri Sembilan DAP requires Loke's experienced leadership to face future challenges, including the 16th General Election (GE16).
"An early analysis of the election results shows that Pakatan Harapan and DAP candidates continue to enjoy strong support from our core supporters despite facing race-based campaigning by our opponents," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saudi crown prince, Trump hold call on Middle East tensions
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman and US President Donald Trump held a call aimed at reducing regional tensions, the kingdom's official SPA press agency reported Sunday.
"His Royal Highness emphasised the necessity of prioritising dialogue to reduce tensions and the importance of exerting all possible efforts to achieve a truce that paves the way for diplomatic solutions," SPA reported after Trump said he had decided to hold off on renewed attacks on Iran after requests from Gulf countries.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lee Lam Thye calls for urgent animal management reforms after dog's death in Klang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Local authorities and state ministries must immediately implement critical reforms to animal management protocols to prevent further cases of animal cruelty, says animal welfare advocate Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye.
He said key measures must include adopting the Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release/Return (TNVR) approach, standardising humane capture techniques, strictly prohibiting private property seizures, and establishing independent oversight committees.
"Municipal councils across Malaysia must immediately abolish obsolete, violent 'catch-and-kill' cycles, which have proven ineffective for decades. TNVR is the only scientifically backed, humane and sustainable method for population management.
"Local councils must formally mandate TNVR policies, partnering directly with recognised animal welfare NGOs and local veterinary networks to manage stray populations humanely," he said in a statement today.
His call follows the recent death of a dog named Rocky in Port Klang, which sparked public outrage over alleged aggressive animal handling during routine enforcement operations.
Lee urged an immediate ban on the use of harsh wire snares, choking loops and other inhumane restraint equipment.
He said enforcement personnel and third-party contractors must undergo certified, mandatory training in non-violent animal handling under the strict supervision of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS).
On private property seizures, Lee said clear operational boundaries must be set and enforced.
"Council personnel and contractors must not seize animals from private residential compounds or home boundaries without written legal notice and owner consultation, strictly respecting property rights and local bylaws," he said.
He proposed that every local council establish an independent oversight committee comprising animal welfare advocates, veterinary professionals and legal representatives to review public complaints, investigate alleged misconduct and ensure compliance with the Animal Welfare Act 2015.
Meanwhile, Lee urged the police, DVS and the Royal Klang City Council to conduct an immediate, transparent and thorough investigation into Rocky's death to ensure swift accountability under the law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pilot held in Indonesia over ecstasy pills smuggling had no prior record
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Indonesia recently for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills had no prior criminal or drug-related record in Malaysia, police said.
Bukit Aman Narcotic Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed this when contacted today.
"Our checks showed that the suspect has no criminal or drug-related record," he said.
Hussein said investigations into the case, including cooperation with the Indonesian authorities, were ongoing.
"We will announce further developments later," he said.
It was previously reported that the Malaysian police would
work closely
with its Indonesian counterparts in the investigation involving the Malaysian pilot, who was arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs into the country.
Hussein had previously told the New Straits Times that police were awaiting more information from the Indonesian authorities before determining the next course of action.
Among the key aspects under investigation are where the suspect allegedly obtained the drugs and whether he was acting on behalf of, or in collaboration with, a drug trafficking syndicate.
Investigators are also looking into how the suspect allegedly managed to smuggle the drugs through airport security in Malaysia before departing for Indonesia.
Hussein said the findings would be crucial in identifying any weaknesses that may have been exploited.
It was reported that the 39-year-old suspect had operated Malaysia Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta
before he was arrested
at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Tuesday night with more than 70,000 ecstasy pills.
He also tested positive for three types of drugs — methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine — after landing in Jakarta.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan exco lineup expected by Friday, says MB
Article:
KUALA PILAH: The lineup of the Negeri Sembilan state executive council is expected to be finalised by this Friday at the latest, said newly appointed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
He said discussions with the Barisan Nasional leadership would be held first before the proposed lineup is presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, for approval.
Ismail said he would also meet Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi soon to seek his views on the composition of the state executive council, including the possibility of appointing state elected representatives from Perikatan Nasional.
"Ideally, we aim to complete the matter within this week, by Friday, if time permits.
"As for Tuanku, His Royal Highness prefers the matter to be resolved as soon as possible.
"We need to form the government together. Naturally, we have state assembly members from BN, not only from Umno but also from component parties MCA and MIC.
"All these factors will be taken into consideration in forming the state executive council," he told reporters at his first press conference after being sworn in as Menteri Besar today.
Earlier, Ismail, who is the Juasseh assemblyman, t
ook his oath of office as Menteri Besar
in a ceremony held before Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.
On the size of the state executive council lineup, Ismail said the matter had yet to be finalised but expressed the view that maintaining a 10-member structure, as practised previously, would be the most suitable arrangement for the state administration.
He said discussions on the appointment of state executive council members and portfolio distribution would only take place after consultations with the party leadership.
"The inclusion of PN assemblymen in the lineup will also be discussed with the Umno president," he said.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the welfare and well-being of the people would remain the state government's top priority during his administration.
He said as a government elected by the people, the well-being of the populace served as the primary pillar and long-term focus of the state administration.
Yesterday's Negeri Sembilan election results saw BN secure 18 seats in the state legislative assembly, while PN won seven, thereby enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls could be held at any time, Rauf hints
Article:
MELAKA: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the Melaka state election could be held at any time following Barisan Nasional's victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
He said the current Melaka state assembly's term expires on Dec 31.
"BN has won two states, so why shouldn't Melaka take the chance?" he said after leading the Sayang Rakyat Tour in the Telok Mas constituency.
Rauf had previously indicated that the assembly would be dissolved "at the right time".
Then, he used the Malay proverb that fruits drop on their own when they are ripe and need not be plucked.
Before this, he said the outcome of the Johor and Negri Sembilan polls would be taken into account in seeking the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly.
The Tanjung Bidara assemblyman said today he was not under pressure to dissolve the state assembly quickly.
He added that there were matters involving the state administration that needed to be settled first.
"In politics, nothing is impossible. Politics is the art of a thousand and one possibilities. Whatever it is, we shall wait and see," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OPEC+ has agreement in principle for September quota increase and pause thereafter, source says
Article:
LONDON: OPEC+ plans to approve a production quota increase on Sunday of around 188,000 barrels per day (bpd) from September, after which it will pause further output increases, sources said, as the group completes the unwinding of voluntary cuts.
The seven core members of OPEC+ — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — have been increasing monthly production quotas for most of this year. Those increases have remained largely on paper, however, as the Iran and Ukraine wars disrupted exports from the Gulf, Russia and Kazakhstan.
After September, the group will likely pause output increases for the rest of the year, one OPEC+ delegate and one OPEC+ source said, as the alliance faces potentially difficult talks over new production quotas.
The September increase would complete a phased rollback of a 1.65 million bpd supply cut originally agreed in 2023, when the group still included the United Arab Emirates, which left OPEC in May.
OPEC+ is carrying out a review of members' oil production capacity to be used for 2027 output baselines, from which quotas are set.
The pause after September would leave in place roughly two million bpd of OPEC+ cuts dating back to 2022 until the group decides how to distribute additional supply among members. Some members of the group, including Iraq, are pushing for higher individual quotas to reflect higher capacity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vietnam's energy-saving drive gathers pace amid soaring summer power demand
Article:
HANOI: Businesses and households across Vietnam are stepping up electricity-saving measures and investing in rooftop solar power as prolonged heatwaves push electricity demand to record levels, Vietnam News Agency (VNA) reported.
The government's efforts to strengthen national energy security are guided by the Prime Minister's Directive No. 10/CT-TTg on electricity saving and rooftop solar development.
At the end of July, Cua Lo Beach in the central province of Nghe An was bustling with tourists. Hotels, restaurants and tourism service providers were operating at full capacity during the peak summer season.
According to the Cua Lo Ward People's Committee, the locality has welcomed more than four million visitors so far this year, up about 12 per cent year-on-year.
While the tourism boom has generated significant revenue, it has also sharply increased electricity consumption.
At Muong Thanh Cua Lo Hotel, occupancy has reached 83 to 85 per cent during the summer months, requiring cooling systems, laundry facilities and other equipment to operate almost continuously.
Vo Huy Tuan, the hotel's managing director, said the hotel has upgraded its equipment, invested in environmentally friendly technologies and encouraged employees to use electricity more efficiently.
Instead of reducing services, it has focused on optimising the operation of major power-consuming systems, particularly laundry and cooling facilities.
"We have adjusted the operating schedule of laundry equipment to avoid peak hours. This helps reduce electricity costs while ensuring sufficient power is available for other services," Tuan said.
Similar changes are taking place at restaurants and tourism service providers, many of which are replacing outdated equipment with energy-efficient alternatives and adjusting the operating schedules of high-power appliances.
Le Anh Tuan, owner of Tuan Phu Quy Restaurant in the Thien Cam tourism site in the central province of Ha Tinh, said monthly electricity bills have fallen by more than 10 per cent after the restaurant adopted power-saving measures recommended by the local power utility, including replacing old air conditioners and lighting systems and requiring staff to switch off unused equipment.
Alongside efforts to improve energy efficiency, many businesses and households are investing in rooftop solar systems as a long-term solution.
Nguyen Van Hung, Vice Chairman of the Cua Lo Ward People's Committee, said nearly 20 per cent of hotels in the locality have installed rooftop solar systems, helping reduce electricity costs while easing pressure on the power supply during the hottest months.
Meanwhile, Le Quang Thanh, Deputy Director of Nghe An Power Company, said the province's peak electricity demand reached about 1,310 MW during heatwaves in May and June, nearly 15 per cent higher than a year earlier.
The company works with local authorities and media agencies to promote efficient electricity use while also providing information and technical advice to households and businesses interested in rooftop solar systems.
Phan Van Nhan from the Can Loc Power Company in Ha Tinh said electricity consumption in the commune surged 24 per cent year-on-year in June due to extreme heat.
To ensure a stable power supply, the utility has stepped up public awareness campaigns and advised customers using more than 1,000 kWh a month to consider rooftop solar systems.
Nhan noted that many high electricity bills stem from wasteful habits such as leaving water heaters on, running air conditioners continuously or keeping lights on unnecessarily.
He also advised households not to set air conditioners at excessively low temperatures, as this increases electricity consumption and shortens the equipment's lifespan.
With electricity demand expected to rise alongside industrialisation, urbanisation and climate change, Directive No. 10/CT-TTg will require the joint efforts of authorities, businesses and the public.
Broader adoption of energy-efficient technologies and responsible electricity use will help strengthen national energy security while supporting Vietnam's green and sustainable development goals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tawau Port acquires two new dock cranes worth RM70mil
Article:
TAWAU: The acquisition of two new quay cranes worth RM70 million for Tawau Port is expected to boost port efficiency and strengthen its role as a key maritime gateway on Sabah's east coast.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the investment is a strategic step to strengthen the state's port infrastructure and support Sabah's long-term economic growth.
He noted that the investment also reflects the state government's commitment through Sabah Ports Sdn Bhd (SPSB) to modernise critical infrastructure, enhancing efficiency and competitiveness of Sabah's ports, particularly on the state's east coast.
"When they become operational, these cranes are expected to improve productivity, operational reliability, and overall cargo-handling efficiency at Tawau Port.
"They will also shorten vessel turnaround times, reduce waiting times, and strengthen the port's capacity to handle larger ships and increasing cargo volumes," he said during the launch of the new cranes at Tawau Port today.
Hajiji emphasised that an efficient and resilient port system is crucial to supporting the growth of key sectors, especially export-oriented industries that contribute significantly to the state's economy.
He said the Tawau Port upgrade is expected to continue fortifying its role as a major maritime gateway on Sabah's east coast, while enhancing connectivity with domestic and regional markets.
The chief minister also praised SPSB, Suria Capital Holdings Bhd, and all parties involved for their ongoing commitment to enhancing the state's maritime infrastructure to support its development agenda.
Meanwhile, Suria Capital chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Dahlan said the investment reflects the group's long-term commitment to developing strategic infrastructure.
"The Tawau Port plays a vital role in supporting trade, industry, and regional relations on the east coast of Sabah.
"This RM70 million investment reflects our commitment to equipping the port with the necessary infrastructure and equipment to meet future trade demands, thereby contributing to the economic development of Tawau and the surrounding area," he said.
Also present at the launch were Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III, who is also the Minister of Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport, Datuk Ewon Benedick; State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, and Sabah Ports Authority chairman Datuk Donald Mojuntin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Discussions with PN in Melaka won't necessarily result in pact, says BN's Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: The winning momentum from Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional's understanding in Negri Sembilan will lead to a "BN Plus" arrangement in Melaka, although discussions with PN may not necessarily result in a political pact.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said the "BN Plus" formula reflected the state chapter's openness to negotiations with any party.
However, he said all decisions would ultimately align with BN's interests and strength in the state.
He said no coalition had been finalised, and Melaka BN remained untethered to any formal political agreement with other parties.
"We are prepared for any form of combination that we call BN Plus. Anyone can come to negotiate, but discussions will not necessarily end with an agreement or consent.
"It depends on our respective strengths. So we are not tied to any binding arrangement that has not been officially finalised.
"I am open to all parties coming to negotiate with me. If I meet anyone, do not make assumptions, because it is our right as a state to prioritise our party's interests first," he said.
He was speaking after leading the Sayang Rakyat Tour for the Telok Mas constituency.
In yesterday's Negri Sembilan election, the BN-PN pact won a two-thirds majority, securing 25 of the 36 seats.
Subsequently, BN chairman
Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
said the coalition's understanding with PN in Negri Sembilan would continue in Melaka.
Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno chief, said BN's consecutive wins in Johor and Negri Sembilan gave the party's machinery a boost ahead of the Melaka polls.
Although the date for the Melaka state election has not been determined, he said BN's victories in the two states provided positive signals of public support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police arrest seven, including two teens, in Jalan Ampang knife‑point robbery investigation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Police arrested seven individuals, including two teenage girls, to assist in the investigation of a knife-point robbery case at a residential unit in Jalan Ampang last Friday.
Wangsa Maju district police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said that the police arrested five men aged 22 to 38 and and two teenage girls aged 13 and 19 in the parking area in Jalan Metro Pudu here at 3 am yesterday.
He said the arrest was made following a report from a 21-year-old man who claimed to have been robbed at knife point by four unknown men while at the residence.
“All those detained have been remanded to assist in the investigation under Section 395/397 of the Penal Code for committing armed gang robbery,” he said in a statement today.
Members of the public who have information related to the incident are requested to contact the District Control Centre of the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters at 03-9289 9222, the Kuala Lumpur police Hotline at 03-2115 9999 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorm warning issued for 10 states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 —The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for 10 states until 6pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected areas are Perlis; Kedah involving Padang Terap, Kuala Muda, Sik, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu; and Perak covering Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim
The warning also covers Kelantan (Pasir Mas, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang), the whole of Terengganu, and several areas in Pahang, namely Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin.
In Selangor, only Hulu Selangor is affected, while in Johor, the areas involved are Batu Pahat, Kluang, Mersing, Pontian, Kulai, Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru.
For Sarawak, the affected areas include Kuching (Bau and Kuching), Betong (Saratok and Kabong), Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu, Miri (Subis, Beluru, Miri and Marudi), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort and Tambunan), West Coast, Sandakan (Beluran), and Kudat. — Bernama

Title: Fire breaks out at Sunway Square Mall, blaze contained before firefighters arrive   (VIDEO)
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 2 — A small kitchen fire at a restaurant in Sunway Square Mall was extinguished even before firefighters reached the scene early this morning, according to the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department.
According to the
New Straits Times
, the department received an emergency call at 1.23am and dispatched a team from the Subang Jaya station. When the first engine arrived five minutes later, the blaze — confined to the cooking hood — had already been put out. Firefighters conducted overhaul work and inspected the premises to ensure no hotspots remained. No injuries were reported.
Eight personnel, a fire engine and a water tanker were deployed. Photos from the scene showed smoke lingering in the kitchen and soot covering the hood, ducting and stainless‑steel counters. The cause of the fire is under investigation.
